rules.claim: Selected preterite-presents have present 1sg=3sg, a special 2sg, and one plural stem/form for all persons; their past is weak. Learn each selected present/past pair as a complete indicative system.
Where Cook prints the past in -e followed by etc., the 2sg adds -st and the plural changes -e to -on. These are declared model-derived cells, not separately quoted textual tokens.
Don, gan, and willan have complete selected present/preterite indicative systems. Gan uses eode for the past; willan has wille in both present 1sg and 3sg, not an automatically added ordinary -ð.
The six beo/bist/bið/beoð indicative person cells supplement the prior wesan system and share its prior past; future or habitual/gnomic state depends on context.
rules.boundary: Productive use is explicitly contextualized expected-later state; no new tense of every verb or future auxiliary willan is inferred.

rules.claim: Second singular commands address one person; second plural commands address more than one. The subject may be omitted or stated.
rules.boundary: Only selected second-person systems are assigned. First/third-person optative commands remain later scope.

rules.claim: Ordinary strong singular imperative is the present stem without the infinitive ending; the second plural normally matches the present indicative plural. Present 2sg/3sg mutation is not mechanically imported into the command stem.

Strong j-presents use weak-I-like -e singular commands: bide, site, lige, hęfe, sciepe, swęre; plurals retain their selected present stems. Hebban/hęfe and licgan/lige require their own consonant alternations.
Don has dō/dōð, gan gā/gāð; wesan/bēon gives wes/wesað and bēo/bēoð. No positive willan command pair or modal command pair is invented.

An earlier supplied dictionary citation does not constitute learned infinitive syntax. Only explicitly selected plain-infinitive cells are promoted; exact prior IDs may be retained with old analysis and history preserved.
rules.boundary: Four defective modal headwords remain citation labels, with no infinitive/inflected target. Unselected earlier lexical rows get no milestone.

rules.claim: For selected -an infinitives the course chooses -anne after tō; -ian therefore gives -ianne and geminated stems remain geminated. Contracted final -n gives -nne: fōnne, sēonne, dōnne, gānne, bēonne. The preposition tō is a separate token.
rules.boundary: -enne is a documented valid variant; selected -anne is not a universal grammatical requirement or a license to derive unattested modal cells.

rules.claim: A finite selected modal/volitional verb takes a plain infinitive in the bounded same-subject construction; the finite verb marks person/number and present/past, while the infinitive does not agree.
rules.boundary: These lexical senses differ. Do not treat every modal as English must, or replace actual indicative past by an automatically hypothetical would/could reading.

rules.claim: Selected cuman + tō + inflected infinitive expresses the purpose of the same subject’s coming. Cook also documents bare infinitives with motion/specification/purpose.
rules.boundary: No claim that all purposes require tō; a valid bare-purpose alternative can miss the stated target without being ungrammatical. General accusative-and-infinitive and dependent-subject syntax remain outside scope.

rules.claim: Ordinary ne before a second-person imperative gives a negative command.
rules.boundary: Construction only; the evidence does not teach ondrǣdan, its reflexive/genitive frame, or a nyllan imperative system.
